tickets.title: NEXT02 — Repair observation hypotheses before granting the harness veto authority
tickets.description:
Active qualification work,12 October. Completed three passive variants over the same eight exact action replays (six P_train experts, two previously inspected learned episodes),1,219 sampled frames per variant. Final physics unchanged, zero action modifications, zero false footprint+yaw goal positives.

Original observer: supported-held precision82.3%, recall99.4%, held-pose coverage67.9%; position p95 12.05mm. Phase/pose circularity causes carried-state errors up to414mm.

Phase-independent prototype: removes large carried-state projection errors, position p95 10.32mm, but a false held detection creates~98mm pose error on a failed-grasp episode. It remains unqualified.

Stereo prototype: camera projection round-trip checks pass. Observable resting-pose p95 is3.03mm; supported-held coverage is0 because the glyph is unavailable simultaneously in both views. This is not a held-pose improvement.

All three fail preregistered qualification. No guard was attached and no authority granted. The2/2 image-transform successes in NEXT03 #10985 use established teacher grasps and a diagnostic handoff, not an autonomous observer trigger. Next is support/depth qualification from visible oblique evidence and robot motion, preserving explicit unknown states and separating ready-to-release from verified completion.

Artifacts: /var/tmp/typhon-research-20261012/observer/REPORT.txt plus all variant traces; backed up to Mint Fast Drive. Existing checkpoints and historical results untouched.

Fourth passive prototype complete: body-centroid stereo support plus numeral yaw has100% precision but6.3% supported-held recall and3.8% held-pose coverage on the same panel. It also fails;2.15mm observed-position p95 mostly measures resting visible poses. All32 replayed episodes are unchanged physically. No intervention is qualified. The next204-suite remains prepared but unrun.

12 October final OST sweep decision
Four passive observation variants evaluated on8exact replays/1,219frames each. No variant qualifies: pose/held precision-recall and phase-transition errors remain. Replay policy/physics unchanged. Do not grant veto or advancement authority. Proceed only with targeted observation repair and a new qualification panel. Evidence:/var/tmp/typhon-research-20261012/observer plus sweep report. Blocker: reliable observable held/release evidence.

OBS05 completed,13 October BST (#11030)
New frozen passive 2×2 component test on the same eight action traces /1,219 observations. Expiring motion evidence reduces contact recall95.8%→83.9% without removing any of eight no-contact false positives. Glyph flow reduces no-contact false positives8→5 but recall falls to51.0%. The old34 supported-lift false positives split into26 actual bilateral contacts below10mm and eight no-contact samples. Keep contact, lift and completion labels separate. None passes the unchanged supported-lift gate; no observer or action authority changed. Full report: https://github.com/NatMota/typhon-robotics/blob/research/obs05-feature-motion/experiment-history/2026-10-13-obs05/REPORT.md
Code/report private branch research/obs05-feature-motion;93 evidence files SHA-verified at /media/nm/Fast Drive/Typhon/research-20261012/obs05/.

OBS06 completed,13 October BST (#11031)
On 24 additional archived episodes /8,784 observations, aperture floor plus measured opening rate reduces false bilateral-contact detections108→20, contact precision77.07%→94.65%, recall96.03%→93.65%. All314 supported-lift samples remain detected. Still fails frozen95% precision; supported-lift precision83.96%. Residual errors include18 partial-gripper contacts and two with none. On original OBS05 development data the rule removes all eight false contact positives, so that result alone would overstate transfer. Keep as a candidate component improvement, not a qualified state/phase observer. No action authority or policy changes. Evidence: https://github.com/NatMota/typhon-robotics/blob/research/obs06-aperture/experiment-history/2026-10-13-obs06/REPORT.md

tickets.title: DATA04 — Validate phone-video to Panda-action alignment beyond one event comparison
tickets.description:
Original request
Earlier user intended video plus geometric-expert supervision, with synchronized views and human corrections retained.

Current evidence / status
One human/expert event timeline is complete, but it is explicitly not eligible as direct per-frame action supervision.

Bounded work and acceptance criteria
Choose training-only examples; preserve native time, embodiment and uncertainty. Align meaningful object events, annotate what is observed versus generated, validate phase transitions and timing before constructing labels. Human pause/reorientation is not automatically a robot motor command.

Dependencies and exclusions
Depends on R07/R09 and calibration. Do not claim original phone footage already has validated Franka labels.

Status semantics
Not running. This ticket records work; creating it does not launch training or change frozen experiments.

12 October final OST sweep decision
Phone-to-robot alignment audit completed; full direct supervision remains blocked. Existing one-clip event alignment has7.6s duration and+-0.25s sync uncertainty; human lift/rotation overlap differs from teacher phase timing. Endpoint retarget succeeds with supplied path/height/timing; it is not full recovered3D. SixP_train tracking sources audited for observable segments, but grasp/release correspondence and metric lift are not established. Proposed reusable object-motion/contact representation recorded; no invented per-frame motor labels. Evidence:audits/phone-alignment-calibration.json.

tickets.title: DATA06 — Version the physical-object and calibration assumptions consistently
tickets.description:
Original request
User identified the orange object as a DUPLO piece and asked to account for dimensions/weight.

Current evidence / status
Frozen experiments use a provisional50×35×30mm,80g proxy although metadata also carries catalogue values. This was disclosed, not silently corrected.

Bounded work and acceptance criteria
Reconcile part identity, catalogue estimate versus actual measurement, physical target scale and camera calibration. Create a new geometry/visual/config version only when justified; validate before rerunning affected scenarios. Keep every old experiment/config immutable.

Dependencies and exclusions
Do not call virtual tabletop millimetres measured human3D. Depends on actual available measurements and intended follow-up scope.

Status semantics
Not running. This ticket records work; creating it does not launch training or change frozen experiments.

12 October final OST sweep decision
Calibration/proxy mismatch explicitly reconciled: frozentraining50x35x30mm,80g versus catalogue32x43x32mm,12.7g; target square virtual100mm. Actual measurements and paired-camera metric calibration remain missing. Do not silently replace geometry or call virtual units physical accuracy. Waiting for measurement/calibration evidence; original results unchanged. Evidence:audits/phone-alignment-calibration.json.

New execution evidence — VIDEO09 #11033: under the declared proxy/camera registration, exact final glyph matching implies a robot centre 27.1 mm from the original goal (tolerance 15 mm). Initial body-derived state and glyph reference differ by 0.1896 target units. This is a feature/proxy registration conflict, not a measurement of the real phone layout. Five physical manipulations all missed the unchanged target. Resolve the contract before treating generated trajectories as teaching data; do not silently move the goal or claim calibrated human 3D.

VIDEO10 #11034 follow-up: one explicit normalized-feature registration to a supplied offline robot-goal image resolves the prior endpoint contract for this proxy, and a shared RGB pre-clock alignment meets the initial feature tolerance. All5matched correction runs pass the original goal. This does NOT supply physical scale, camera calibration, measured dimensions or human3D. Remaining observer-versus-projected-asset position discrepancy is about0.076normalized units; its cause is unresolved. tickets.title: R01c — Show exactly what V4 sees: 512→224 images, crop and six history frames
tickets.description:
**Original request**

What does 2×1 pixels mean, where does shrinking occur, why do earlier images matter, and what image is actually in the system?

**What was verified**

Audited the actual saved V4 release query, original inference response and independent benchmark receipt. Saved actual current/history images, native-resolution panels, a clearly labelled magnification and a plain-language explainer. No model inference or source modifications were needed.

**Measured input pipeline**

The simulator provides two full 512×512 RGB views, overhead and oblique. The pinned image processor resizes these to 224×224. O2 additionally attempts a 96×96 overhead orange-object crop, resized to 224×224 if detection succeeds. The release crop was absent: the current mask was [true, true, false]. No secondary-camera crop fallback exists.

The 2×1 measurement is the bounding box of one thresholded connected blue fragment associated with the numeral in the current oblique image. tickets.title: R01b — Measure V4's numeral sensitivity and grasp-relative orientation response
tickets.description:
**Original request**

Can we establish whether V4 failed to recognise or use the blue 2 / correct orientation when it released the brick?

**Interpretation**

Separate sensitivity to the visual marking, correct directional use, grasp-relative wrist compensation and conflicts between visual and numeric instructions. Changing actions does not by itself establish semantic numeral recognition.

**Completed experiment**

Frozen V4, checkpoint SHA-256 c884e5052bc2734c1edf7d33498497cb26b27d88db1b32e3289fc46ea2e453dc, on Powerglide RTX4090. 78 offline predictions across three archived states from one film-demo_0006 episode, plus nine separately frozen coherent-goal predictions. Three paired diffusion noises per condition are repetitions, not independent scenes. No new training or physical rollouts.

Original/sham/blank/90°/180°/270° renderer-level numeral conditions; current-only versus history-consistent changes. Physical state, collision geometry, cameras, lights, proprio and noise are fixed. Baseline RGB replays match the archive exactly. Sham inputs/actions are bitwise identical. All 12 overlapping initial outputs exactly reproduce the earlier controlled probe.

The actual tokenized instruction includes both 'orient its blue 2' and numeric body yaw 0 with a fixed numeral convention. Numeral-only rotations can contradict that convention. The nine-query addendum therefore updates persistent numeral appearance AND numeric body goal/convention consistently. Updated text survives tokenization; no additional numeric goal input was found. Original baseline outputs are reused by hash. These remain unusual counterfactual appearances/goals and are not an in-distribution benchmark.

**Results**

• Initial 180° numeral changes move the predicted wrist endpoint by 26.13–33.72° and position by 82.61–90.45 mm. V4 is locally sensitive to the marking.
• At the held state, altering current and past numeral views barely changes the proposed motion. Updating the goal consistently still produces endpoint wrist yaw 93.98–94.32° and opening at waypoint 11 for all nine conditions.
• Coherent +90°/+180°/+270° glyph offsets require wrist yaw 84.15°/−5.85°/−95.85°. Predicted glyph error at opening is 8.32–8.83° / 98.33–98.86° / 171.09–171.66°. The first case happens to align with the near-common motion; it does not show adaptation.
• The original unchanged goal requires wrist yaw 174.15° for the measured grasp. V4 targets 94.77–95.11°, implying about 79° endpoint error; it proposes opening with about 81° error. These are fixed-grasp implications of raw proposals, not newly achieved trajectories.

**Conclusion and limits**

Initial cue dependence is established. The full system fails to adapt its held-state orientation proposal to these coherent goals. The unchanged numeric instruction alone does not explain the near-common response. This does not locate the cause in perception, language conditioning or action mapping, nor establish general numeral understanding. That unresolved attribution remains open in R01f.

**Artifacts and verification**

Powerglide: /var/tmp/typhon-research-20261011/blue2-causal-20261011-v1 and blue2-causal-20261011-v2-coherent-goal.
Mint archive: same branches under /media/nm/Fast Drive/Typhon/research-20261011.
Saved protocols, exact tensors/masks/history, task text, paired noise, raw/decoded actions, grasp-relative scoring, contact sheets and reproduction commands. V1: 551 files / 84,797,655 bytes; V2: 58 files / 10,114,485 bytes. Every manifest entry was SHA-verified on Mint. Reports and mint-verified.json receipts inspected. GPU workers exited.

**Separate work**

[R01f #11011](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=11011): locate the perception/conditioning/action cause.
[R01c #10955](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=10955): actual image/history explanation.
[VIS01 #10993](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=10993): qualify a visibility fix.
[R01 #10957](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=10957): original physical release trace.

tickets.title: R01f — Separate lost visual detail from failure to use orientation in the action head
tickets.description:
**Original request**

Establish why V4 does not correct the brick's orientation; distinguish perceiving the blue 2 from choosing the right wrist action for the actual grasp.

**Established evidence**

R01b completed 78 controlled visual-cue predictions and nine coherent image/goal predictions. Rotating the initial visible numeral by 180° changes the proposed wrist endpoint by 26–34°. At the held/release state, consistent current/history numeral changes barely affect the proposal. Updating the numeric goal and numeral convention together also leaves nearly the same ~94° wrist endpoint and opening time across three very different goals.

This establishes local cue dependence initially and a held-state failure of the combined goal-to-action system. It does not distinguish weak visual encoding, ignored language, a dominant learned motion sequence, insufficient examples of the actual grasp, or their combination.

**Bounded next work**

After reviewing the frozen R01b evidence, select a controlled representation/visibility diagnostic. Compare exact current/history visual features and, if justified, a clearly labelled high-visibility view. Keep physical pose, proprio, goal and paired noise fixed; include original and sham. Preserve the distinction between information that is decodable and information that causes the policy's action. Any crop/input change must be qualified and labelled potentially out of distribution.

**Acceptance**

Determine which component-level claims the measurements support and which remain unresolved. A generic action change is not proof of correct semantic interpretation; a weak change is not proof the encoder cannot perceive the numeral. No new model training is implied.

**Dependencies**

[R01b #10954](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=10954), [R01c #10955](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=10955), [VIS01 #10993](http://127.0.0.1:4001/?project=typhon-research#ticket=10993).

24-hour plan: original /sham /obscured /clearer numeral input probes at approach, grasp and release with fixed state and paired inference noise. Evaluate correctness relative to required wrist pose, not merely action change. Extra crop remains diagnostic until train/inference consistency is qualified.

12 October OST traversal: implementing frozen V4 representation/visibility probe using existing replay-qualified original/sham/blank/rotated numeral packets. Compare encoded feature changes and action correctness with fixed state/noise, then high-visibility crop diagnostics. No training or physical-pose changes in this test.

108 frozen V4 predictions completed across three saved states, six cue variants, two image presentations and three paired seeds. Enlarging the visible held numeral fragment increased auxiliary-feature sensitivity (180-degree cue change: relative L2 0.0102 to 0.1887), but required-wrist error remained about80 degrees and opening stayed at waypoint11. tickets.title: VIDEO08 — Test whether existing views identify camera geometry for a video-to-robot adapter
tickets.description:
Continuation of VIDEO01 #11015 / DATA06 #10991, frozen before numeric results.
Question: do the existing M0 target-square image annotations identify camera geometry well enough to justify dimensionless 3D retargeting, without new measurements or geometric-expert paths?

Inputs: exact M0 primary/secondary four target corners and original export sizes; canonical 90-degree CCW primary transform explicitly inverted for raw-image geometry. No claim that hand-drawn target is a measured exact square. One target plane per camera, unknown intrinsics, no independent metric dimensions. Use source code and hashed phone frames as provenance. Existing P_train/holdout unchanged; no learned fit or action labels.

Method: quantify the two orthogonality/equal-norm focal constraints under explicit centred-principal-point, zero-skew, square-pixel pinhole assumptions. Sweep a predeclared focal/FOV range and principal-point offsets; fit planar pose using generic PnP and report models whose maximum corner reprojection discrepancy lies inside M0's stated 5px corner uncertainty. Report camera height and tilt in target-side units, not metres. Perturb corners with fixed seeded +/-5px input sensitivity; do not call a sensitivity envelope a confidence interval. Verify camera/coordinate implementation against an exact synthetic pinhole construction and independent projection. Preserve rejected/ambiguous fits.

Decision: only consider a dimensionless stereo adapter if camera geometry is constrained enough under the declared assumptions; otherwise retain image-space motion as an observation and explicitly reject uncalibrated metric/3D labels. The focal sweep is a sensitivity analysis, not proof of the cameras' physical parameters. No policy training, paid compute, robot truth, GE motion labels or alteration of frozen M0 outputs.

Artifacts: separate research/video08-calibration-identifiability branch/worktree; protocol, numeric candidates, sensitivity summary, annotated source references, reproducible script and report. Lightweight CPU audit on archived Mint files while expired Powerglide reservation is renewed; subsequent GPU execution only when access returns.

User request12October: add an OST experiment to understand a generic robot encoder and compare methods driven by personal video, not the existing geometric teacher.

Interpretation
Separate the human-video representation from the robot-specific action decoder/controller. A universal robot encoder is a hypothesis, not an existing component. Keep original footage and frozen models/results unchanged.

Arms
A: track object-centric motion, directed orientation and observable contact events from phone frames.
B: track hand/pinch motion and aperture from phone frames, with uncertainty through occlusion.
C: use frozen pretrained visual features over the actual human sequence to represent temporal progress/subgoals; test whether they preserve task-relevant motion across views and distinguish correction from completion.
Existing endpoint/geometric expert is a labelled comparator only, not labels or trajectory generator forA/B/C.

Acceptance
Audit actual available calibration, synchronization and source split. Preserve full source timestamps and feature provenance. Run paired-view correspondence, temporal reversal/shuffle/static-video negative controls, and held-out take/view tests. Where justified, retarget one observed trajectory to Panda using only declared calibration, robot kinematics/controller and task-independent feasibility constraints. Record every supplied constant. Do not invent metric3D, hand contacts or robot-action labels from2D. If calibration blocks motor execution, report the representation-level result and blocker explicitly rather than silently substituting teacher waypoints.

Generalisation
Distinguish representation reuse across layouts/views from motor transfer to another robot. Freeze any second-robot or novel-layout test before execution. No new paid compute, no model upgrade or publication.

All models pick up both development cases. Mean fixture distance P 267.69 mm, F 240.67 mm, FL 6.30 mm. Both independent expert feasibility controls pass. All 12 physical starts and actual first RGB policy arrays match exactly across models. A separate preview has five one-level pixel differences; originals retained.

Stable released feeding placements remain 5/6 for all. Shared source 0001 grasps/lifts but stalls in a held state: late policy targets stay local, gripper remains closed, controller tracks them. Joint-limit causality and numeral understanding are not established.

tickets.description:

Panel: exact final LOAD01 FL checkpoint; unchanged loading scenes demo_0012 and demo_0013; exact LOAD02 feeding/loading requests; native visible versus fixture visually suppressed; paired seeds 912171/912172. Total 16 policy rollouts. No training, F model, harness, new prompts, thresholds or extra conditions.

Suppress only fixture_floor and fixture_wall_0 through fixture_wall_3 from both policy camera RGB images via renderer visibility. Preserve physics, contacts, seat height, dynamics, lighting/cameras, brick/numeral, robot, green feeding marker, domain, proprioception, H30/native controller and scoring. Do not paint over images, erase foreground, remove collisions, add simulator truth to actor inputs or change crop logic. Record native RGB-derived crop decisions and masks.

Before execution: freeze exact geometry list; native no-op RGB/tensor parity; render/physics/input isolation; correct foreground occlusion; initial crop decision parity; existing feeding/loading training-reference visibility audit. Actual noise/RNG checks remain paired. Separate 60-minute clock after LOAD02 closure: qualification by 20 minutes, execution stops by 50, archive/report by 60. Stop if clean visual-only intervention cannot qualify; do not start a renderer repair programme.

Score both physical endpoints independently, requested versus wrong versus neither, pickup/transport, distances, initial proposals and paired instruction switching. A switch under both instructions indicates dependence on fixture appearance, not semantic language control. Failure to grasp indicates visual disruption. Continued loading narrows only this cue hypothesis. The invisible-but-physical fixture is a diagnostic observation intervention, not a deployment fix.

tickets.description:
Question: Does removing the training correlation between fixture visibility and task make feeding/loading instructions select the requested destination?

Basis: LOAD01 added loading competence; LOAD02 found no instruction switching; LOAD03 completed 16/16 physical endpoint placements but only 8/16 requested-task successes. Visible fixture selected loading and suppressed appearance selected feeding under either instruction in two development scenes.

Protocol from Hm challeng p2, 2026-10-13:
- Separate 120-minute window. Data/render gate by +30 min; both endpoints and exact reload by +85; evaluation by +110; verified closeout by +120.
- Exact sealed FL parent, SHA-256 76334b9a17ac5fc49f46c2cb850a3c39ef38e0f13b9cdadc324f760567c5f128.
- Eight strict-qualified trajectories, feeding and loading for each training parent 0001/0002/0003/0005. Paired tasks share fixture-present physical configuration/reset and initial native images/proprioception. Up to eight total expert generation/replay executions; no replacements or rescue reseeding. Stop if any pair fails qualification.
- Render visible and hidden variants with the qualified LOAD03 renderer-only intervention. Preserve physics and action labels. No 0012/0013 actions or counterfactuals enter training; no quarantined correction data.
- Two equal-budget full-joint continuations, fresh identical optimizers, existing LOAD01 settings/domain29, batch four, seed141901, 3,000 updates, final endpoints only.
- Identical frozen 12,000 family/task/window draws: 1,500 per parent/task. C correlated control hides the fixture for feeding and shows it for loading. B counterbalanced gives each parent/task 750 visible and 750 hidden presentations. Same underlying eight trajectories, not additional independent demonstrations.
- Original LOAD03 development panel for each checkpoint: 0012/0013, two original instructions, visible/suppressed, seeds912171/912172. H30 and both strict destination scorers unchanged. 32 new rollouts; archived FL results historical only.
- Primary: successful two-way instruction switching, /4 matched pairs separately per visibility. Also requested/wrong/neither endpoint rates, pickup and strict placement. These are inspected development configurations.
- Stop on failed qualification, nonfinite training, failed reload, storage failure or time cap. No extra conditions, checkpoints or automatic extensions.
Interpretation: B outperforming C supports improved selection from counterbalanced supervision; equal improvement leaves shared data/additional training explanations; weakened cue dependence alone is not instruction control; lost manipulation is no useful improvement; neither switching means this recipe insufficient.

tickets.title: LOAD05-Q — Repair content signatures and qualify saved-action restart
tickets.description:
**Yes. EXECUTE LOAD05-Q: a verifier-only repair followed by the minimum saved-action restart qualification. Separate output directory and a 30-minute cap.**

The XML address strings establish a verifier defect. **They do not establish that the original restoration was otherwise correct**, because its post-restore signature was not saved. Keep the stopped LOAD05 attempt classified as **failed qualification, with zero crossover results**.

## 1. Repair serialization—not restoration

Change only the signature canonicalizer and diagnostic logging. Leave state capture/restoration, controller code, physics, observation order and numerical tolerances unchanged.

For recognized XML element types, compare deterministic **XML content**, not `str(Element)` or object addresses. Preserve tags, attributes, child order, text and relevant namespaces. Standard XML libraries provide serialization/canonicalization specifically for content-based comparison. Do not strip text, discard attributes or reorder child elements to obtain equality. [Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.etree.elementtree.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Do not apply a general “remove hexadecimal addresses” filter.** Unknown opaque types must be explicitly reported rather than silently ignored. Do not carry forward the earlier `meansize` exception unless independently relevant and already declared in this verifier.

Before every assertion, persist:

- Independently captured **before and after** state records, including raw XML and numerical arrays.
- Canonical signatures and their schema version.
- Field-level differences, including missing keys, shape/dtype changes and numerical differences.

Confirm that the saved “before” record does not share mutable storage with the restored environment.

## 2. Mandatory copy-only tests

Run these before creating a simulator:

| Test | Required result |
|---|---|
| XML element versus its deep copy | New content signatures equal, despite different object identities |
| Change a geometry attribute in the copy | Signature differs; diagnostic identifies the exact field |
| Change child order or meaningful text | Difference retained—not normalized away |
| Change one element of a synthetic numerical state array | Full-state verifier detects it and saves both values |
| Unsupported opaque object | Explicit unsupported-field result, not assumed equivalence |

These tests qualify the comparator. They do **not** qualify an actual simulator restart.

## 3. At most two saved-action restart checks

Freeze the repaired verifier before these checks. Use the existing **C and B demo0012/loading/visible-fixture/seed912171** archives, branching at the already-selected **tick100/query2**.

For each source, once:

1. Replay its archived prefix to tick100.
2. Capture the complete pre-restore state.
3. Apply the **unchanged** copy/restore procedure.
4. Save the complete post-restore state and field-level comparison before asserting.
5. If the state check passes, execute **the next 30 archived actions** with the original observation/render call order; compare against the corresponding archived trace.

**No model loading or inference is needed.** No crossover, extra `forward()`, new seed or controller adjustment belongs in this qualification.

Retain full physical/controller checks, including controls, applied forces, warm-start state, cached quantities and command history. XML-content equality cannot replace those checks: MuJoCo’s continuation can depend on actuator, callback and solver state beyond positions and velocities. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/programming/simulation.html)

## 4. Decision gate

| Result | Action |
|---|---|
| Both content/state comparisons and saved-action continuations pass | **Restart qualification passes for the repaired verifier and these states.** |
| XML content matches but another state field differs | Save the exact difference and stop; no quiet exclusion or tolerance change |
| State signature passes but the continuation diverges | Restoration remains unqualified; preserve the first divergence |
| Tests or qualification cannot finish within 30 minutes | Close with the specific blocker; no repair-and-retry loop |

**A successful new qualification does not retroactively prove that pointer strings were the original attempt’s only discrepancy.**

On a pass, **proceed without another approval round to the already-authorized LOAD05 pre-contact crossover**, in a new, separately frozen execution namespace: the same two states, C/B checkpoints, paired noise and maximum four 90-step continuations. Preserve its original scientific question and existing execution cap; add no conditions.

The immediate work is therefore **content-safe signatures → recorded before/after evidence → two restart checks**. This repairs a demonstrated measurement defect without weakening the physical gate or turning a failed restart into model evidence.

Predecessor stopped LOAD05 #11044; no prior crossover result. Separate worktree, branch and namespace; Powerglide compute, Mint FastDrive backup. On a pass, continue the already-scoped crossover without another permission request.

tickets.title: LOAD05-R — Reconstruct pre-contact states and cross C/B acquisition policies
tickets.description:
## EXECUTE NEXT: LOAD05-R — deterministic-prefix crossover, not native pickle

**Use the reset-plus-prefix route. Do not spend another qualification cycle on copying or pickling live physics.**

Yes: **independently reconstructing the same branch state can support the causal comparison**, provided the physical/controller state, actor inputs and native continuations pass the checks below. The requirement is equivalent execution conditions—not identical allocator contents or memory addresses.

The two stopped attempts remain **restart-qualification failures, not model results**. My earlier all-public-arrays comparison was too broad: it failed to distinguish valid simulation fields from solver-conditional or undefined storage.

## 1. Freeze a semantic state comparator first

Allocate **at most ten minutes**, using the pinned MuJoCo 2.3.7 source already available locally. Do not repair the simulator.

Record the actual solver, integrator, Jacobian mode, relevant flags, timestep and active sizes. Replace indiscriminate public-array hashing with a versioned field manifest:

| Category | Comparison rule |
|---|---|
| **Physical and controller state** | Retain positions, velocities, actuator state/control, applied forces, warm-start state, mocap/user state, controller references and other behavior-relevant wrapper state |
| **Active contacts and constraints** | Compare their valid, populated contents—not merely counts |
| **Derived kinematics/render state** | Compare at the same native computation point, without recomputing them |
| **Solver-conditional fields** | Include only when defined for the actual solver and computation stage; exclusions require a pinned-source justification |
| **Process identity/diagnostics** | Structural XML comparison; separately record excluded addresses, wall-clock timers and other nonbehavioral metadata |

MuJoCo’s documented state includes more than qpos/qvel: callbacks, controls, mocap and solver warm-start information can affect continuation. Those remain part of qualification. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/programming/simulation.html)

For `efc_AR*`, **do not infer inactivity from strange numbers alone**. Check `mj_isDual(m)` and the pinned allocation/computation path. MuJoCo identifies PGS as dual and CG/Newton as primal. Exclude these fields only when the actual path establishes that they are uncomputed and unused here. Apply the same reasoning separately to sparse-storage metadata. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/APIreference/APIfunctions.html)

**Do not exclude all `efc_*` arrays.** The documented contact/constraint arrays have different meanings and active extents; `efc_J`, forces, constraint state and associated populated fields cannot be dismissed because a different buffer is inactive. Compare engine-defined live ranges, not unused capacity. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/APIreference/APItypes.html)

Preserve the old raw dumps and document every exclusion **before any new continuation**. Do not zero buffers, change the solver or add initialization calls to make signatures agree.

## 2. Reconstruct each branch by executing its history

Use a new private namespace and protocol. Preserve:

- Exact LOAD04 **C and B checkpoint hashes**.
- **demo0012, fixture visible, loading instruction, seed912171**.
- Original reset procedure and **60 archived pre-branch actions**.
- Branch boundary **tick100/query2**.
- H30, native timing, preprocessing, controller and original numerical settings.

For each branch, create an independent environment, perform the normal reset, and replay its source model’s archived prefix through the **same adapter/controller path**. Keep that simulator instance alive and continue in place.

**No live-state copy, pickle restore, `mj_setState` shortcut, direct pose injection or extra `forward()`.** Preserve the original observation/render call order: recomputing cached quantities at a different point can change which state the cameras and controller observe. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/programming/simulation.html)

Reconstruct the nonphysics context too: previous-target proprioception, query index, pending-action cursor, instruction and any native image/history buffers. Do not replace a mismatching current render with an archived image to force an input match.

At tick100, require:

- No prior gripper–brick contact.
- The block remains upright and within the existing pre-acquisition tolerances.
- Recorded physical/controller fields and actual prepared inputs match the source archive under the **already-frozen** comparison rules.

Copy numerical arrays into independent diagnostic records when saving them. MuJoCo’s Python bindings expose mutable underlying memory; retaining array views can otherwise make an earlier snapshot change as simulation advances. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/python.html)

## 3. Four branches total; diagonals first

Each branch gets its own fresh reset and source-prefix replay:

| Order | Prefix source | Continuation checkpoint | Role |
|---:|---|---|---|
| **1** | C | C | Qualify native C continuation |
| **2** | B | B | Qualify native B continuation |
| **3** | C | B | Test B from C’s pre-contact state |
| **4** | B | C | Test C from B’s pre-contact state |

This gives **two independently reconstructed prefixes per source**, without adding separate repeat-only rollouts.

Use the archived noise tensors for the corresponding query indices, identically across checkpoints within each source-state pair. Confirm actual inputs and noise before inference. Do not generate extra queries merely to advance RNG.

Run **90 control steps after the branch point**, at most three generated chunks per branch. No settling extension, rescue, guard or final-task evaluation.

### Diagonal gate

Before either crossed continuation runs, both diagonal branches must match their archived:

- Prepared inputs, noise and raw predictions.
- Applied commands and physical/controller traces.
- Acquisition-phase behavior, including the upright-versus-tipping distinction.

Matching only “C upright/B tipped” is insufficient.

### Independent-prefix gate

Before branch 3 or 4 queries its alternative checkpoint, compare its reconstructed tick100 state and complete input packet with the corresponding saved diagonal branch.

For active cache fields absent from the original LOAD04 archive, report **agreement between the two new prefix reconstructions**, not invented historical equality. The diagonal’s archived input/action/trajectory agreement supplies the complementary execution check.

**Do not require C’s state to equal B’s state.** Their difference is the factor being crossed.

## 4. What counts as an equivalent branch state?

For this experiment, accept **qualified prefix reconstruction** when:

1. The original recorded state and actor inputs are reproduced.
2. Two independent reconstructions of each source prefix agree on the defined behavior-relevant state.
3. The matching-checkpoint continuation reproduces the archived trajectory under the original tolerances.

That is sufficient to run the prespecified crossover. **It is not certification of native copying/pickling, byte identity of every memory location, or universal determinism.**

If any currently read behavior-relevant field remains unexplained, stop. Do not move it into the exclusion list because it differs.

## 5. Outcomes and interpretation

Keep the original acquisition measurements: first contact geometry, finger aperture and command, requested/measured approach, relative velocity, tilt trajectory, bilateral contact and supported lift.

| Crossover pattern | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|
| B tips from both source states; C remains upright from both | B’s post-boundary action policy is implicated |
| Both tip from B’s state, both remain upright from C’s | The earlier approach state is implicated |
| Outcome depends on both | A state–policy interaction |
| Either diagonal fails qualification | No crossover conclusion; preserve the first divergence |

A prefix state includes pose, velocity, aperture, command history and observation context. A state-following result does **not** isolate one millimetre offset or one contact force.

The new branches remain diagnostic continuations, outside LOAD04 success counts and all training data.

## 6. Time cap and stop rules

**One 60-minute window:**

| Boundary | Required progress |
|---|---|
| **T+10 min** | Comparator manifest, source justifications and protocol frozen |
| **T+30 min** | Both native diagonal branches qualified |
| **T+45 min** | Both crossed branches finished |
| **T+60 min** | Analysis and verified private archive |

Stop at the first unexplained active-state, input, noise or trajectory mismatch. Save both sides and field-level differences **before asserting**. No solver change, tolerance widening, alternate seed, pickle fallback or repair-and-rerun loop.

**Proceed with LOAD05-R.** The objective is to answer why B tips the brick before acquisition—not to turn this project into a general MuJoCo checkpointing investigation.

Separate follow-up to stopped LOAD05 #11044 and failed LOAD05-Q #11045. Private branch/worktree; Powerglide compute, Mint FastDrive evidence. Earlier outputs stay unchanged.

## APPROVED — EXECUTE LOAD05-R2 with only the two missing crossovers

**Reuse the qualified C→C and B→B diagonals. Four fresh branches are unnecessary.** Preserve R as a stopped attempt; R2 is an explicit follow-up with one narrowly defined comparator amendment.

MuJoCo 2.3.7 documents `statistic.meansize` as the length scale for visualization decorations, with no other side effect. That supports excluding this attribute from physical-equivalence comparison, **while retaining the camera/input checks**. Do not exclude the whole `statistic` element: other attributes have different semantics. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/XMLreference.html)

### Freeze this amendment before inference

| Item | R2 requirement |
|---|---|
| **Only new exclusion** | The `meansize` attribute of the XML `statistic` element, identified structurally—not by the fragile child index `4` |
| **Preservation** | Save complete original XML, both values and raw fingerprints. Change the comparison only; do not modify either live model’s value |
| **Runtime** | Same execution code as R except the comparator/manifest change; same checkpoint, configuration and environment hashes |
| **Other checks** | Preserve every existing physical, active-constraint, contact, controller, history, RNG and input check, with unchanged tolerances |
| **Usage qualification** | Cite the existing local usage audit confirming no custom actor/controller dependency on `meansize`; retain exact fixed-camera RGB and prepared-input equality |

### Reuse the diagonals explicitly

Reference R’s exact diagonal artifacts and qualification results in R2. Re-evaluate their **saved comparisons** under the amended comparator without rerunning physics.

Label them **“qualified controls reused from LOAD05-R,”** not newly executed R2 controls. Their passed archived predictions and trajectories remain valid evidence.

### Execute exactly two fresh independent-prefix branches

| Branch | Reconstruction | Continuation |
|---|---|---|
| **C→B** | Native reset plus C’s exact archived prefix to tick100/query2 | B for **90 steps** |
| **B→C** | Native reset plus B’s exact archived prefix to tick100/query2 | C for **90 steps** |

Before each first crossed query, compare the reconstructed state and actual prepared tensors with its **corresponding source diagonal**. Only the declared `meansize` difference is newly permitted. Keep the same archived per-query noise, H30, observations and controller.

**After the checkpoint swap, different predictions and trajectories are the experimental result—not a parity failure.** Continue checking actual noise injection and execution contracts, but do not require B’s predictions to equal C’s.

### Stop and report

Set a **20-minute R2 cap**. Stop at any additional unexplained pre-branch difference, failed input/noise qualification or runtime error. No new exclusions, tolerance changes, retries or simulator-copy fallback.

Report the four-cell acquisition table using the two inherited diagonals and two new crossovers, with contact, tilt, bilateral acquisition and supported-lift events. Do not add final-placement claims or benchmark counts.

**Proceed now. The demonstrated visualization-metadata difference should no longer block the actual acquisition question.**

tickets.title: LOAD05 — Pre-contact C/B acquisition crossover
tickets.description:
Amended BEFORE any LOAD05 simulator execution, 14 October. The planner superseded its initial post-grasp proposal after the completed read-only LOAD04 phase audit. This is a pre-contact acquisition diagnostic, not a placement evaluation.

**Yes—move LOAD05’s branch point to before first contact. Replace the unexecuted post-grasp crossover; do not add another experiment.**

Your trace localizes the failure much earlier than my previous proposal assumed: **the brick is already tilted approximately 61–62° when bilateral contact begins, and 63–64° at the first supported lift.** Release does not initiate the failure. The small commanded and actual wrist-axis tilt also argues against a large wrist-roll error.

The next question is therefore about **approach, finger-contact geometry and acquisition timing**, without yet assuming which offset or command causes the tipping. A post-grasp crossover would primarily test recovery from an already-tipped object.

## EXECUTE NEXT: LOAD05 — pre-contact C/B crossover

Seal LOAD04 first. Freeze this amendment before any LOAD05 outcomes. Keep **visible-fixture demo0012, loading instruction, seed912171**, and the exact C/B checkpoints.

### 1. Select one common branching time

From the archived C and B traces, identify the **last shared native query boundary strictly before the first gripper–brick contact in either execution**.

At that boundary, require both bricks to remain upright and within the existing post-reset position/stability tolerances.

**Do not use “before step110” as the rule:** step110 is when tilt crosses 15°, not necessarily when the contact that initiates rotation begins. Do not insert an off-schedule query.

Save each model’s complete state at this same control tick:

- \(S_C\): C’s pre-contact state and native input packet.
- \(S_B\): B’s pre-contact state and native input packet.

### 2. Run the four crossed continuations

| Starting state | Continue with C | Continue with B |
|---|---|---|
| **\(S_C\)** | Native C reference | Does B’s next behavior cause tipping from C’s approach state? |
| **\(S_B\)** | Can C acquire upright from B’s approach state? | Native B reference |

Use the archived matched noise sequence at corresponding query indices. Within each row, the checkpoints receive identical starting observations, proprioception, instruction and controller state.

**Run at most 90 control steps—three native chunks—from the branch point**, with no added settling, correction, guard or expert intervention. This is an acquisition diagnostic, not a final-placement evaluation.

If the two complete states and input packets are identical, collapse duplicate rows and run only the two distinct checkpoint continuations.

### 3. Qualify restoration, not a new controller

Retain the existing allowance of **at most two short saved-action prefix qualifications**. Verify the prepared tensors and complete physical/controller state, including warm-start and actuator state—not just qpos/qvel. These additional state components can affect MuJoCo’s subsequent execution. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/programming/simulation.html)

The diagonal continuations—C from \(S_C\), B from \(S_B\)—must reproduce the corresponding archived phase behavior within the established qualification tolerances. If they do not, stop the crossover interpretation; do not rerun until the desired tipping pattern appears.

## Evidence to record

Use simulator geometry only for **offline measurement**, never as a new actor input.

| Measurement | Purpose |
|---|---|
| First contacting robot geom, contact location and brick face | Identifies the actual contact geometry |
| Finger aperture and opening/closing command | Separates an open-finger collision from intended closure |
| Requested versus measured approach motion | Distinguishes policy proposal from tracking |
| Finger-to-brick offsets and relative velocity immediately before contact | Tests approach differences without treating the EEF site as a fingertip |
| Tilt trace, first threshold crossing, bilateral-contact time and lift orientation | Establishes when acquisition becomes compromised |
| Full acquired grasp transform, where a supported grasp occurs | Distinguishes upright pickup from successful retention of an already-tipped brick |

## Decision gate

| Pattern | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|
| B tips from both states; C remains upright from both | B’s post-branch action policy is implicated |
| Both remain upright from \(S_C\), but both tip from \(S_B\) | Earlier approach state—pose, velocity, aperture or command history—is implicated |
| Results depend on both checkpoint and starting state | A state–policy interaction; not one universal bad offset |
| Neither diagonal reproduces the archived behavior | Restart qualification failed; no causal conclusion |

These comparisons will not isolate a particular millimetre offset or prove contact causality by themselves. They identify **which part of the execution to modify next**.

**Keep the separate 60-minute LOAD05 cap. No new scenes, seeds, hidden-fixture conditions or training.** The destination-selection gain remains valid; the newly localized defect is acquisition quality in demo0012. **Trace and test that first—not release timing.**

tickets.description:
**This is a state–policy interaction, not a uniformly bad B approach state or a uniformly bad B acquisition policy.** B acquires upright from C’s state, and C acquires upright from B’s state. Only their original B-state/B-policy combination tips the brick in this inspected case.

**Next priority: separate the pose sequence from the gripper-closing schedule at that failing boundary.** Do not add training or a release guard.

## 1. Preserve R/R2 first; Mint’s power state remains unknown

Seal the raw results, manifests and code on Powerglide and push the permitted small reports/manifests privately. **Do not describe that as a completed Mint backup.** The next physical test should wait for a checksum-verified independent copy on Mint, or another already-authorized backup destination.

For Nat, the accurate status is:

> **Mint is unreachable through the tested SSH routes; whether it is awake is not established. Earlier verified backups remain intact as last verified. R/R2 are currently preserved on Powerglide.**

Preparing the following protocol and inspecting existing action arrays can proceed while connectivity is resolved. Do not restart Powerglide or discard its live evidence to troubleshoot Mint.

## 2. EXECUTE NEXT once preservation clears: LOAD06 — pose × gripper-schedule crossover

**One case, one starting state, at most four 90-step continuations. No training.**

The question is:

> **Does the pre-acquisition tipping depend on B’s approach pose sequence, its gripper schedule, or their combination?**

“Other runs first contact under CLOSE” does not alone establish that B should close earlier. Their slower/different approaches may simply reach the brick later. We need to manipulate the two command components separately.

### Use two existing proposals from the *same B state*

Take the first 30-waypoint chunks at **tick100/query2** from:

- **B→B:** B’s proposal from B’s pre-contact state.
- **B→C:** C’s proposal from that same B state.

**Do not use C’s proposal from C’s own state.** That would reintroduce the input-state difference we just isolated.

Both donor chunks already have qualified input/noise provenance. Freeze their exact hashes.

### Four conditions

All four reconstruct **B’s identical pre-contact state** using the qualified deterministic reset-plus-prefix route.

| Condition | First-chunk XYZ and full wrist rotation | First-chunk gripper schedule |
|---|---|---|
| **BB — native reference** | B | B |
| **BC — grip-only substitution** | B | C |
| **CB — pose-only substitution** | C | B |
| **CC — complete donor chunk** | C | C |

“Pose” includes the complete XYZ/rotation sequence. This experiment does **not** separately isolate descent speed, lateral offset and wrist orientation.

Use the native output-to-command conversion unchanged. Swap only the designated active-arm channels; retain the original inactive-arm handling. Preserve continuous gripper predictions and the resulting applied OPEN/CLOSE sequence in the record.

**Do not invent an earlier close, slow down either trajectory, interpolate between models, or choose a schedule after seeing outcomes.**

### Continue with B after the first chunk

At the next normal query boundary, return **every condition to checkpoint B** for the remaining 60 steps, with the archived matched noise at corresponding query indices.

The resulting observation and proprioception must reflect what that branch actually executed. Preserve the existing previous-target convention; do not supply the original B target history after executing a different pose sequence.

This preserves B as the continuing policy while testing a **single-chunk acquisition intervention**. It remains a diagnostic hybrid—not an autonomous B success or a production repair.

## 3. Qualify and score the two time intervals separately

### Before physical execution

In a maximum ten-minute array audit, record when the donor pose and applied gripper schedules first differ.

- If their gripper schedules are identical through tick110, their differences cannot explain the *earlier* tipping onset under an otherwise identical pose stream.
- If complete command streams and handoff inputs are identical for two conditions, collapse that duplicate rather than running it twice.
- Do not manufacture a stronger intervention to obtain a more decisive contrast.

Use LOAD05-R2’s accepted comparator unchanged, including only its documented exclusions. Preserve active controller and solver state; MuJoCo continuation depends on controls and warm-start state as well as positions and velocities. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/programming/simulation.html)

Run BB first. It must reproduce the archived B→B behavior. CC’s **first 30 steps** must reproduce the archived B→C first chunk; after that it uses B rather than C, so later equality is neither required nor expected. Stop on a qualification failure—no new serialization investigation inside LOAD06.

### Primary endpoint: the first 30 steps

This isolates the immediate effects of the selected pose/gripper combination before a new policy query.

Record maximum object tilt, first contact, first closing command, measured aperture, contacting geom/pad, contact location and relative approach velocity. Use the existing contact instrumentation; MuJoCo exposes contact geometry identities, positions and frames for this offline analysis. [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/APIreference/APItypes.html)

### Secondary endpoint: the complete 90-step segment

Record whether B subsequently achieves a supported lift while retaining the existing upright tolerance, plus tilt and grasp-relative orientation. Separate:

- Preventing initial tipping.
- Acquiring an upright grasp.
- Preserving that grasp under subsequent B control.

**No final-placement or strict-task-success claim:** this segment does not evaluate the complete task.

## 4. Decision gate

| Result | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|
| BC prevents initial tipping with B’s pose sequence | Gripper scheduling contributes causally in this local combination |
| CB prevents tipping with B’s gripper schedule | The pose sequence contributes; speed versus lateral geometry remains unresolved |
| Both substitutions work | Two alternative local interventions are sufficient—not one uniquely identified cause |
| Only CC works | Coordinated pose/gripper behavior matters; neither isolated substitution is sufficient |
| Initial tipping is prevented, but later B control loses upright acquisition | The first-chunk repair is insufficient for the subsequent phase |
| Qualification fails | No new causal result; preserve the exact failure |

This is one selected development state and noise realization. It cannot establish a universal “close earlier” rule.

## 5. Cap and data boundary

**Separate 45-minute clock, beginning after the preservation prerequisite:**

| Boundary | Work |
|---|---|
| **T+10 min** | Donor-array audit and protocol frozen |
| **T+35 min** | At most four continuations finished |
| **T+45 min** | Analysis, private report and verified archive |

No new model generation is needed for the first chunk; at most eight subsequent B queries are needed across four branches. Keep seeds, task text, fixture visibility, controller, H30 and physics unchanged.

**All resulting hybrid traces remain development diagnostics, quarantined from training.** A successful intervention could identify what to seek in future *training-family* corrections, but it must not become a new imitation target merely because it repaired this inspected case. Learner-state corrective training requires appropriate supervision and an explicit dataset boundary. [Proceedings of Machine Learning Research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v15/ross11a.html)

**The priority order is: preserve R/R2 → inspect the two saved command streams → test this one-chunk pose/gripper crossover.** B’s demonstrated task-selection gain stays intact; we are isolating its acquisition failure without replacing the whole policy or beginning another training cycle.

tickets.title: INIT06 — paired hold/loading references at actual learner q1 states
tickets.description:
## EXECUTE NEXT: INIT06 — paired preservation/loading supervision at the actual q1 learner state

**Start with demo0001, then expand to demo0002 only if the first pair qualifies. Maximum four continuations, no training.**

INIT05 supports this choice: **changing the wider-view image input is sufficient to trigger the large approach proposal locally; the approximately 10 mm proprioception change is not.** The unchanged crop rules out its *change* as the cause of this particular contrast. It does not establish which feature in the wider views matters, or that the crop is irrelevant elsewhere.

The next useful step is therefore **not freezing images or modifying proprioception**. It is testing whether we can supply two valid, contrasting actions from the **real state whose images trigger initiation**:

- Feeding request: preserve the already-completed arrangement.
- Loading request: acquire the block and complete loading.

This is a data-qualification experiment, not evidence that T has learned either decision.

## 1. Freeze the two source states

Use T’s archived **feeding-preservation executions**, policy seed **912171**, from INIT02:

| Stage | Parent | State |
|---|---|---|
| **Principal pair** | **0001** | Exact **q1** packet used in INIT05, immediately before its second policy query |
| **Conditional second pair** | **0002** | Its corresponding archived **q1** boundary, selected now—not by later correction success |

These are training-family states generated after T’s first 30 commands. Retain the actual inherited physical state, including velocity and controller state.

For each parent, require before branching:

- No preceding gripper–block contact.
- No meaningful block displacement from the completed starting arrangement.
- The original feeding endpoint still passes.
- Loading remains unsatisfied.
- The required archived actions, native inputs and state records are available.

**If the specified q1 state is ineligible or unavailable, do not replace it with another query, seed or parent.** Record the limitation.

The second family is a check against a one-example result—not independent scene diversity. Your existing source geometry remains tightly concentrated.

## 2. Reconstruct the state through its actual history

For each continuation, independently execute:

```text
Original qualified INIT01 feeding prefix
→ original T q0 action chunk, replayed from its archived commands
→ stop immediately before q1 inference
→ qualified hold or loading continuation
```

**Do not load T to regenerate the prefix.** No new VLA query is needed. Do not inject q1’s joint/object poses, reset the controller or return the arm to its original rest position.

Use the established deterministic-prefix implementation and semantic comparator, including only its already-documented exclusions. Preserve warm-start, control, contact and controller state—not merely qpos/qvel. Those additional inputs can affect MuJoCo continuation. [Mujoco Documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/2.3.7/programming/simulation.html)

### Two distinct provenance checks

1. **Historical reconstruction:** compare against every available archived q1 state field and the original actual prepared inputs.
2. **Paired branch equality:** record complete new states for hold and load, and compare those using the unchanged comparator.

Do not claim historical equality for fields that were never archived. If the existing records and prefix checks cannot qualify the boundary without another reconstruction investigation, stop this block with that specific gap.

## 3. Execute the two branches from the same q1 state

| Branch | Instruction recorded for supervision | Controller |
|---|---|---|
| **F-preserve** | Exact original feeding/preservation instruction | Fixed measured-pose hold with gripper open |
| **L-teacher** | Exact corresponding loading instruction | Unchanged nominal geometric loading expert qualified in INIT01 |

**Keep the original instructions, including their existing wording.** Do not insert H-explicit or silently remove “grasp” language. That would introduce a second proposed repair.

This establishes references under the project’s supplied task semantics. It does not resolve whether the inherited wording is the best way to express those semantics.

### F-preserve: 60 real control ticks

At q1, capture the **measured full end-effector pose once**. Hold that fixed pose with the gripper open through the same qualified conversion/controller used for INIT01 preservation.

- Do not update the target to the latest measured pose every tick.
- Do not hold the raw previously predicted target instead.
- Do not overwrite the existing low-level controller state.
- Record every actual observation and command for all 60 ticks.

Keeping the existing three-second procedure avoids simultaneously changing both **the initial state** and **the hold duration**. A successful hold qualifies this short supervision record; it does not prove full-horizon policy preservation.

### L-teacher: complete loading from the current state

Run the **unchanged nominal scripted loading expert** used successfully in INIT01. It must calculate its actions from the current reconstructed state, not replay the old q0 loading trajectory.

Retain its existing attempt limits, gains, grasp convention and transfer/release routine. No extra home motion, staging repair, delay, changed grasp or new controller.

The original request has already consumed 30 of its 1,460 post-reset ticks. **At most 1,430 remain, including the final 24 settling ticks.** Do not provide a fresh full horizon.

Keep the teacher’s actual active checks. Do not attach the unrelated zero-tolerance joint guard. Record limit excursions, phase convergence and contact behavior explicitly.

## 4. Preserve the learner’s actual input convention in the candidate records

This is essential: the new supervision must begin at **the q1 input that T actually received**, not a freshly initialized approximation.

For the first record in both branches:

- Preserve the exact q1 images, O2 masks and effective previous-target proprioception.
- Change only the task instruction between the paired supervision requests.
- **Do not replace q1’s inherited proprioception with measured reset proprioception or canonicalize its 6D values.**
- Record measured robot pose separately.

Generate each new action label through the existing qualified:

```text
absolute_target(normalized_command, measured_pre_action_observation, config)
```

After the first action, use the existing recorder’s command-history update convention. Retain both executed normalized commands and reconstructed absolute labels so the boundary is auditable.

The loading expert may use simulator object truth, as already declared. **That truth must not enter the recorded learner observation, prompt, crop or proprioception.** The hold branch uses measured robot pose and its supplied no-action decision.

These are now **learner-visited-state corrective candidates**, unlike INIT01’s expert-terminal-state bank. That is closer to the data-collection principle of DAgger, but no iterative dataset aggregation or retraining has occurred yet. [Proceedings of Machine Learning Research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v15/ross11a.html)

## 5. Qualification gates before expanding

Run **F-preserve first, then L-teacher** for parent0001. Assess the pair before starting parent0002.

| Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---|
| **Shared starting information** | Actual prepared nontext tensors match the archived q1 packet and match across the two branches |
| **Preservation** | Original feeding score passes; no gripper–object contact; maximum block displacement ≤1 mm; uprightness and stability preserved |
| **Loading acquisition** | Bilateral supported lift ≥70 mm while within the original upright tolerance for at least three consecutive 20 Hz samples; retain the full interval |
| **Loading completion** | Original strict loading endpoint passes, including orientation, footprint, height, seating, release and stability |
| **Teacher quality** | Relevant phases converge; no hidden intervention or runtime failure. Record any joint-limit excursions rather than suppressing them |
| **Labels** | Correct pre-action timing, actual complete H30 windows, valid action conversion and no terminal padding |
| **Behavioral contrast** | The loading suffix contains verified task-directed transport; the preservation record remains physically non-manipulating |

For **automatic candidate admission**, require the same clean teacher qualification achieved in INIT01, including no observed joint-limit excursion. An otherwise successful execution with an excursion remains a documented, **unqualified candidate**—not a reason to alter runtime limits or retry.

**Only if the complete0001 pair qualifies, run the identical two-branch procedure for0002.** No third or fourth family in this block.

## 6. What the paired outcomes decide

| Outcome | Decision |
|---|---|
| Both pairs qualify | We have task-contrasted supervision at two actual early learner states where the original hold distribution was inadequate. A narrowly matched repair-training proposal is justified next |
| Hold qualifies, loading teacher fails | Do not teach blanket inactivity as the solution; the positive loading action reference is missing |
| Loading qualifies, hold fails | The preservation reference is not qualified from this moving state; do not admit a misleading no-action label |
|0001 qualifies but0002 does not | One local candidate, not a qualified multi-parent repair bank |
| Input/replay or label alignment fails | Infrastructure/data-contract blocker, not evidence against task-conditioned learnability |

**Do not judge the pair solely by whether its first 30 labels differ strongly.** The teacher may initially align before transporting. Report where the qualified sequences first diverge and which complete windows contain that divergence. Do not shift labels backward in time to make loading look more distinguishable.

The result would show that suitable corrective actions **can be supplied from these states**. It would not prove that T can learn the distinction, that imagery is the only relevant conditioning variable, or that the original instructions are unambiguous.

## 7. Boundaries, time and the next decision

**Separate 60-minute clock, starting after INIT05’s verified archive:**

| Boundary | Work |
|---|---|
| **T+15 min** | Both specified source-state identities, protocol, storage and reconstruction approach qualified |
| **T+35 min** | Principal0001 pair complete and scored |
| **T+45 min** | Conditional0002 pair complete |
| **T+60 min** | Independent scoring, compact candidate manifest and verified archive |

Maximum **four continuations**, plus their recorded prefix reconstructions. No new native-policy rollouts, R restore, weights, teacher variants or retries.

Keep all source prefixes and raw branch traces. Write new files to a **candidate-only bank**; no active training manifest changes. Offload sealed per-parent outputs to Mint and verify hashes before reclaiming scratch. Preserve the margin before **16 October 01:00 UTC**.

If both pairs qualify, automatically prepare—but do not launch—a small repair proposal identifying:

- Which matched state/instruction examples would be added.
- How existing loading and feeding skills would be rehearsed.
- How an equal-budget control would distinguish new-state supervision from more optimization.
- A full-horizon preservation evaluation, since short teacher holds are not that test.

**Proceed with INIT06.** The objective is to turn the localized image-driven initiation failure into a small, physically verified **“same state, different requested task, different correct behavior”** dataset—not to suppress motion with stale images or begin another broad training run.
